MoonPay Enterprise is for builders with something to prove.

This isn't a "work on cool crypto stuff" company. It's a high-standards, high-velocity, high-accountability company building the operating system for value movement. If the internet moves information, we move value: crypto, stablecoins, tokenized assets, and whatever comes next. Four offerings make that real: fund, tokenize, trade, and spend.

MoonPay Enterprise is the fund layer built for businesses. We power how stablecoins move through real financial operations: enterprises, fintechs, PSPs, wallets, and marketplaces running their treasuries, their cross-border flows, and their stablecoin operations on us. The goal is to make moving real money at scale as predictable as any other piece of financial infrastructure, with the compliance and controls CFOs need to say yes.

AI is the default operating mode here. It's woven into every role, and we expect you to use it daily. It handles the manual work so you can deliver on what actually matters.

You'll thrive here if outcomes excite you more than process, if impact motivates you more than titles, and if you want hard problems, real ownership, and teammates who love winning, building, and doing it together.

The bar is high. The pace is real. We're building the rails that businesses run real money on, for humans and agents. MoonPay ranked #2 in Crypto Services on Fortune's inaugural Crypto 100, made Forbes' America's Best Startup Employers 2026 (Top 25 in Finance), and landed on The Sunday Times Best Places to Work two years running.


About MoonPay Enterprise

MoonPay Enterprise is one of the more operationally complex products in the stablecoin space: multiple banking providers, multiple payment rails, a growing partner base across two product lines (Orchestration and Issuance), and an active compliance surface across each. MoonPay Enterprise runs B2B, B2B2B, and B2B2C models. Partners integrate our API. Their customers become direct customers of MoonPay Enterprise for compliance purposes.

KYB is the front door. Every partner is a business. Every business customer of every partner clears KYB before a single transaction moves. Today the flow is part automated registry verification, part manual review, with different rules for the US and the rest of the world, and turnaround measured in days. That does not scale to where MoonPay Enterprise is going. KYB has to become a product: measurable, fast, API-first, defensible in front of regulators and banking partners. This is a principal seat. You set the multi-year direction for how businesses enter MoonPay Enterprise, and you own the outcome.

What You'll Own

KYB product strategy & roadmap

  • Business onboarding end-to-end, across every model MoonPay Enterprise runs: partners onboarding onto MoonPay Enterprise, businesses onboarding directly, and business customers onboarding through partners.

  • Platform altitude. KYB decisions ripple into KYC, Travel Rule capture, banking-provider onboarding, and Issuance partner diligence. Connect the surfaces; don't optimise one in isolation.

  • MoonPay Enterprise runs three KYC delivery models (reliance, outsourcing, hosted). KYB coverage is uneven across them. You decide where it expands and in what order.

  • Genuine product depth on MoonPay Enterprise is non-negotiable. Within weeks you talk fluently about KYB outcomes, UBO requirements, virtual account structures, and API behaviour. From being hands-on, not from documentation.

Onboarding funnel & conversion

  • The KYB funnel is yours: pass rate, time-to-verified against a 48-72h target, manual review rate, drop-off per step.

  • Instrument what isn't instrumented. Make approval speed and rejection quality measurable. Then move both.

  • Fix rejection UX. Today a declined business often gets a status without a reason, and the partner escalates to support to find out what is missing. Rejection reasons, retry semantics, and resubmission flows become API surface partners build on.

KYB API & partner experience

  • The KYB API surface: statuses, webhooks, document submission, and the edge cases that make business onboarding hard (sole proprietors, corporate shareholders, one person who is UBO, Director, and Representative at once).

  • Partners integrate KYB in weeks and self-serve their onboarding questions. Every "what is missing for this customer" escalation is a product gap. Close it.

Compliance as product

  • Turn compliance-approved onboarding matrices into product logic. US and non-US differ: control prong versus directors, when ownership documents are required, self-certification options. Partners should never need to read a matrix.

  • EDD triggers, high-risk classification, prohibited industries, Travel Rule capture: you decide how they show up in the product.

  • Compliance is your sparring partner, not a ticket queue. You shape how policy becomes product. They own the policy.

Vendor & provider orchestration

  • The verification stack (SumSub today) and the build-versus-buy calls around it.

  • Cost per verification, automation rate, vendor performance. Know when a second provider, a waterfall, or in-house tooling earns its place.

  • Push automation. Decide where AI-assisted review with a human in the loop replaces manual queues, and prove it does not raise risk.

  • Every new banking provider brings its own onboarding requirements. Keep KYB compatible with every rail without collecting everything from everyone.

Who You Are

  • A principal-level PM with real KYB or KYC depth. You have owned onboarding, identity, verification, or risk as a platform, not a feature.

  • High agency. You do not wait for a mandate, a brief, or perfect data. You find the problem, claim it, and fix it.

  • Full autonomy, zero to one. Hand you an unowned surface and you take it from first principles to shipped. No handover document, no waiting for direction.

  • AI-fluent by default. AI tools are your daily instruments for analysis, prototyping, and drafting. You run your own queries; analysis is not something you request from another team.

  • Compliance is a design constraint, not a blocker. You read a requirements matrix and see API design, funnel steps, and copy.

  • You know your funnel cold: pass rate, time-to-verified, manual review rate, cost per verification.

  • At home in API-first B2B. Your users are partner engineers and the businesses behind them, not consumers.

  • You have run verification vendors (SumSub, Persona, or equivalents) and know when to switch, stack, or build.

  • A multiplier for the product team around you. You raise the bar for how compliance-heavy product work gets scoped, specced, and shipped.

  • Bias to action. Reactive stewardship of an existing flow is not what we are hiring for.

 
NYC Salary: $217,000 - $279,000

Research has shown that women are less likely than men to apply for this role if they do not have experience in 100% of these areas. Please know that this list is indicative, and that we would still love to hear from you even if you feel that you are only a 75% match. Skills can be learned, diversity cannot.

Frontline work keeps the world running. Restaurants, hospitals, schools, nurseries, airlines, stores, emergency services. Together they employ 80% of the global workforce, over 3 billion people, and they're among the hardest businesses anywhere to run. By-the-minute scheduling, HR and payroll make them far more operationally complex than the average office, yet just 1% of venture funding has ever gone to software built for them.

 

Rising costs, wage increases, labour shortages and tighter regulation have made fixing that urgent. Sona is the AI-native workforce management platform for frontline organisations, with agents that match staffing to real demand and take the admin load off managers. That's a $500bn+ market the software industry has mostly walked past.

 

We've raised over $100M from N47, Felicis, Gradient and Northzone, signed more than 100 enterprise customers across the UK and US, and opened offices in London, New York, Austin and Lisbon. More on working at Sona here.

 

About the Role

 

We're growing our payroll bureau fast and looking for a Payroll Manager to lead a team of Payroll Specialists, driving accuracy, compliance and client experience across their portfolio. This is a people-management role: you'll coach and develop your team, own escalations, and stay hands-on with payroll when it matters.

You'll also be a driving force behind automation and continuous improvement, using AI to cut manual effort and building best-practice, auditable payroll flows as you go.

 

Responsibilities

If you’re ready to help build Europe’s leading platform for property operations — and make a tangible impact on how the real estate industry works — join SINGU and be part of this transformation.

The Opportunity

SINGU provides property and facilities management technology for organisations operating complex, multi-site estates. Retail is a strategically important market for the business, spanning shopping centres, retail parks, high-street portfolios, supermarkets, hospitality and other distributed consumer environments.

We are seeking an experienced retail property, facilities or operations leader to become SINGU's senior market authority for retail and help build a differentiated, commercially successful position in the sector.

The Retail Market Principal will combine deep industry expertise, executive credibility and market leadership with clear commercial accountability. The role will help SINGU determine where it has the strongest right to win, create access to senior decision-makers, originate strategic opportunities, accelerate priority deals and strengthen SINGU's relevance across the retail property and facilities ecosystem.

This is not a conventional sales, pre-sales, product marketing or communications role. It is a senior, market-facing position for someone who understands retail property and operations at practitioner level and can translate that experience, credibility and network into measurable commercial impact.

Success will be measured not simply through market visibility or activity, but through SINGU's ability to create qualified pipeline, win strategic customers, expand existing relationships and establish a repeatable position within priority retail segments.

What Success Looks Like

Within the first 12 months, you will have established a clear and credible retail go-to-market strategy, identifying the segments and use cases where SINGU can win disproportionately and building meaningful executive relationships across priority retail accounts.

You will have originated and influenced significant qualified pipeline, contributed demonstrably to both new-logo and expansion revenue, and developed repeatable retail propositions supported by clear customer evidence.

You will also have strengthened SINGU's network of retail customers and advocates, while materially increasing our credibility, relevance and market position within the retail property and facilities sector.

What You Will Own

Retail Market Strategy:

  • Define where SINGU has the strongest right to win across retail.

  • Shape our retail go-to-market strategy, priority segments, use cases and target accounts.

  • Maintain a strong point of view on the operational, regulatory and technology issues shaping retail estates.

  • Translate market insight into clear commercial and product priorities.

Executive Access and Market Development:

  • Build trusted relationships with senior leaders across retail property, facilities, operations, asset management and transformation.

  • Use your network and industry credibility to create access to strategic prospects and originate new opportunities.

  • Represent SINGU in executive forums, customer meetings, roundtables and selected industry events.

  • Build relationships across the wider retail ecosystem, including advisers, FM providers, managing agents and partners.

Strategic Accounts and Commercial Impact:

  • Work with Sales and Customer Success on a focused portfolio of priority retail accounts.

  • Help uncover strategic priorities, strengthen business cases and improve executive engagement.

  • Support selected opportunities where your involvement can materially increase SINGU's probability of winning.

  • Identify expansion opportunities across customers, countries, sites, modules and use cases.

  • Contribute directly to qualified pipeline and revenue growth, without replacing the accountable salesperson.

Customer and Market Insight:

  • Build a strong community of retail customers, advocates and industry influencers.

  • Bring structured market insight into Product, Product Marketing and Commercial Strategy.

  • Identify repeatable customer needs, emerging opportunities and gaps in SINGU's proposition.

  • Help ensure SINGU invests in problems that customers are willing to pay to solve.

Commercial Accountability:

This is not a conventional quota-carrying role, but it has clear commercial accountability. Performance will be measured against:

  • qualified pipeline originated and materially influenced;

  • revenue contribution from strategic retail opportunities;

  • progression and penetration of priority accounts;

  • executive relationships created within target organisations;

  • development of repeatable retail propositions and use cases;

  • customer advocacy and market influence.

What We're Looking For:

  • First-hand understanding of complex, multi-site retail estates.

  • The opportunity to shape SINGU's retail market position across Europe.

Mission

Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear.

In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives.

Role Purpose

The Member Experience Training & Quality Coordinator makes the Neko member experience standard real on the ground. You deliver our member experience training to teams across the business, primarily clinic teams and centralised support teams, and you run the quality assurance activity that tells us whether the standard is actually landing in practice.

This is a delivery role at the heart of a live culture change programme. You will facilitate training that shifts mindset, not just process, run experience audits against CARE and the Member First Manifesto, and turn what you see into coaching and improvement. As markets scale, you keep the standard consistent across every site and cohort, and rising over time.

You own the coordination and logistics that keep training and quality assurance running: scheduling sessions and audits, and organising the people, spaces and materials each one needs. You report to the Hospitality Programme Lead and support the wider rollout, so you will also play a hands-on part in projects and launch activity as new clinics and teams come online.

What You’ll Deliver in the First 6–12 Months

  • Stage 1 and Stage 2 member experience training delivered consistently to every new clinic cohort in your market, with 30-day reviews showing the mindset shift is landing, not just attendance being logged. (Member First, always)

  • A regular quality assurance rhythm is live: experience audits across clinic and support teams, scored consistently against CARE and the Member First Manifesto, with clear findings shared back to the teams and their leads. (Impact, not activity)

  • Audit insight turned into action: recurring friction points named early and at least two concrete experience improvements implemented with clinic and support leads. (Optimistic truth-seeking)

  • Support team training built out and delivered alongside clinic training, so centralised member support holds the same standard as the clinic floor. (Chase 10X, not 10%)

  • The ongoing learning ecosystem running smoothly, including the monthly AI role play and quiz, with completion tracked and shared with Clinic Leads as a coaching tool, not a performance measure. (Tech-enabled, human-centred)

  • A training and audit calendar owned end to end: sessions scheduled around clinic rotas and cohort timing, facilitators, rooms, materials and joining details arranged, and audits planned on a set cadence so every site and team is covered without gaps. (Impact, not activity)

Minimum Requirements

  • 3+ years in training delivery, learning and development, hospitality, or member and customer experience, ideally in a high-touch service, hospitality, or premium retail environment.

  • A confident facilitator, comfortable leading a room of clinicians and operators and holding attention and energy across a full-day session.

  • Hands-on experience running quality assurance or experience audits, mystery shopping, or service standard reviews, with the ability to score consistently and give feedback that changes behaviour.

  • A sharp eye for service detail and what separates a good experience from an exceptional one, drawn from service design and hospitality thinking rather than process alone.

  • Organised and self-directed, able to run a training and audit calendar across multiple sites and cohorts without dropping the standard.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, and the credibility to influence teams and leads who do not report to you.

  • Willingness to travel regularly between clinic sites, and occasionally between markets.

  • Experience supporting a multi-site clinic, hospitality, or retail rollout as it scales.

  • Experience with digital learning tools, an LMS, or AI-enabled training and assessment.

  • Confident with everyday workplace tools, including Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, Excel and Outlook, to build training materials, track audits and report findings.

Hiring Process

Candidates progress from application and structured screening through thoughtfully designed interviews culminating in a formal offer and final pre-employment checks before joining the team.

Equal Opportunity & Inclusion Statement

Neko Health is committed to inclusive hiring and member-first care. We welcome candidates from all backgrounds and encourage you to request reasonable adjustments to support your application.

At PPRO, we simplify access to local payments - providing a local payments platform that empowers giants like PayPal, Stripe, and Microsoft to connect with billions of consumers worldwide. We are on an ambitious, fast-paced mission to 3x our growth by 2028 - and we’re just getting started.

Our magic lies in our team of proud payments nerds. Spanning over 50 nationalities across 10+ global locations, our diverse cultures aren't a checklist; they are the competitive advantage driving our innovation. This is a people-first, high trust environment where you’ll have the autonomy to make a massive impact, own your work end-to-end, and grow through broad exposure, meaningful challenges, and continuous learning. We get things done, challenge respectfully, put the customer first, and recognise that our biggest successes are those we create as a team. If you’re ready to leave your footprint on global commerce, join us.

The Purpose:

PPRO’s Digital Workplace team strives to enable every employee to do their best work. We aim to provide a delightful, innovative, and secure IT experience. Our Colleague Support Engineers are at the forefront of that effort, assisting our colleagues with their IT needs, challenges, and issues throughout their journey with PPRO.

As our vibrant London office continues to expand, you will serve as the primary IT ambassador on the ground. From resolving critical login issues to optimizing office connectivity for high-stakes collaboration, you'll be the trusted expert your colleagues rely on every day.

In addition to owning end-to-end first and second line support locally, you will collaborate closely with our global support hubs in Munich, Berlin, and São Paulo to drive consistent, high-quality standards across all PPRO locations. You'll play a key role in fostering a supportive, solution-driven workplace culture.

  • Deliver exceptional 1st and 2nd line IT support to empower our London team, while collaborating on global support initiatives

  • Provide white-glove IT support services to executive team members, ensuring rapid resolution and seamless experience for critical business operations

  • Administer access management via Okta and terraform to ensure secure, seamless employee onboarding and daily operations

  • Manage the full macOS and Windows device lifecycle, ensuring endpoints are secure, up-to-date, and performing optimally

  • Drive innovation by introducing modern AI productivity tools, such as Claude, to help team members optimize daily workflows

  • Champion the IT employee lifecycle, driving memorable onboarding experiences for new starters and smooth offboardings

  • Optimize office network connectivity and audio/visual hardware across meeting rooms and workstations to enable effortless collaboration

  • Author and refine knowledge base documentation, encouraging self-service problem solving across the organization

  • Partner with vendor networks to streamline local hardware procurement, software licensing, and repair management

  • Proven track record in IT support, with equivalent practical experience or a relevant degree

  • 3+ years of experience resolving complex technical issues in dynamic environments

  • Ability to work onsite in our London office 5 days a week (must be UK-based with right to work)

  • Strong communication skills in English, both written and spoken

  • Solid background supporting enterprise macOS and Windows operating systems

  • Familiarity with enterprise platforms such as Okta, Google Workspace, Intune, Jira, or Workspace ONE


    • Nice to Have:

  • Prior experience in customer-centric roles or technical support desks

  • Experience with M365 and Dynamics

    • What's in it for you?
     
    Holiday - We offer 28-day holiday allowance.
     
    Learning and Development - We offer a GBP 1,000 annual budget to support your professional growth—because investing in your development benefits us all. In addition, we provide leadership cafés, on-the-job training, and other opportunities to help you grow your skills and thrive in your role..
     
    Insurance - Because better safe than sorry - we want our employees to benefit from various insurances including a medical insurance (BUPA health care plan) and a 5% matching pension plan through Now Pensions.
     
    Enhance Family Leave - We understand the importance of family - that's why we offer enhanced family leave to support you during key life moments.
     
    Workplace Nursery Scheme - Save on childcare through salary exchange
     
    Gym membership - PPRO helps contribute towards the costs of your gym membership, supporting your physical fitness journey while easing the burden on your wallet
     
    Mental Health Platform - We’ve teamed up with a top well-being platform to provide one-on-one therapy, chat therapy, therapist-led courses, guided meditations, and more.
     
    Our HQ office on Procter Street, is a short walk from Holborn, Farringdon and Covent Garden so if you’re a foodie there’s plenty nearby. The office is befitting a tech business and is set up for cross team collaboration.
     
    Pet-friendly office- Because work is better with your paw-tners by your side

    We get things done: We are courageous; we take ownership, make decisions and get things done.
     
    We act with trust and integrity: We listen first and challenge respectfully. We seek out and leverage diverse perspectives. We welcome and offer honest and open feedback, always assuming positive intent
     
    We put the customer first: We are laser focused on delivering outstanding outcomes for our customers. We put the customer at the heart of what we do.
     
    We make things better: We boldly explore  new ideas and have an unwavering commitment to continuous improvement.
     
    We work as a team: We collaborate closely and value team success over individual achievement.

Relay is fundamentally reshaping how goods move in an online era. Backed by Europe’s largest-ever logistics Series A ($35M), led by deep-tech investors Plural (whose portfolio spans fusion energy and space exploration), Relay is scaling faster than 99.98% of venture-backed startups. We're assembling the most talent-dense team the logistics industry has ever seen

Relay’s Mission is to free commerce from friction. Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. We envision a world where more goods move more freely between more people, making the online shopping experience seamless and accessible to everyone.

THE TEAM
• ~110 people, more than half in engineering, product and data
• 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research
• Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle
• An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking, tight feedback loops and relentless experimentation

The Opportunity

You will report to the Site Manager/Head of Site and will run shifts at one of our Hybrid Sort Centres (HSCs), leading 50–100+ operatives through high-volume, time-pressured sortation where minutes matter and small deviations cascade into missed deadlines. Each of our HSCs handle over 40 million parcels annually, with our largest site measuring more than 300,000 sq ft.

You will also be accountable for whether the site is measurably better in a month than it is today for each of our key metrics. You are on the floor for your shift, every shift. This is not a project role with occasional site visits and it is not a desk job, the forward work happens along with running the operation.

 

Who will thrive in this role

  • Deliver shift plan end to end people deployment, throughput, quality standards, and health & safety compliance

  • Lead, develop, and performance-manage a frontline team of 50–100+ operatives

  • Build the mechanisms that hold the operation together. Build controls, cadences, metrics, SOPs, change management and own their adoption, not only their design

  • Plan ahead for future shifts; labour, training, and the risks you can see coming before they land

  • Own the end-of-shift handover; what happened, what is at risk, what the next shift needs to know

  • Stay decisive through volume peaks, outages, and labour gaps. Triage, solve the problem at hand quickly, contain the impact, restore flow

  • Present and write clearly whether briefs, escalations, handovers or post-incident reviews. Decisions here get made based off what you wrote

  • Implement changes into a live operation such as introducing robotics, launching new sortation tech or onboarding new clients. We are changing the operations constantly which means you’ll roll change out mid flight and bring your team along the journey.

 

Who you are

  • Scaled something from zero: a site, a market, a process or a program.

  • Managed a physical operation: quick commerce, grocery, e-commerce fulfillment, last mile, 3PL, food production, airport ground handling, rail. Anywhere with a hard cut off and people on the floor.

  • Communicate in both directions and have strong people management skills: you can brief 80 operatives at shift start and take a problem to senior leadership the same day.

  • Built a mechanism that held: a control, a cadence, a metric, a document standard. Something you authored that changed how frontline teams worked.

  • Own numbers rather than report them: you can name a metric you created or redefined, explain why the previous one was wrong, and say what changed afterwards.

  • Understand frontline work: one of these must be true: you have personally led frontline teams; you have worked embedded in and around a frontline population day to day, without the reporting line; or you have been accountable for outcomes delivered by frontline people you did not employ.

You do not need to have worked in parcels, fulfilment, or sortation. Several of our most talented people had not.

 

Backgrounds that translate well

  • Program Manager in a logistics or e-commerce business

  • Operations Excellence and Continuous Improvement

  • Strategy & Operations

  • Transformation manager

  • Launch and Expansion Manager

  • Regional operations manager

We have hired well from corporate operations, from central operations inside large UK retailers and carriers, and from quick commerce and marketplace operators. Consulting backgrounds work where you implemented, not only recommended; we are keen to understand what you who actually rolled it out.

 

Hiring process

Our hiring process is fast.

  • Initial screen (15 min)

  • Hiring Manager conversation (90 min) - 45 min onsite interview immediately followed by a 45 min site tour where you shadow an existing shift manager

  • Final interview (45 min). Decision and offer within 48 hours

Who Thrives at Relay?

  • Aim with Precision: You define problems clearly and measure your impact meticulously.

  • Play to Win: You chase bold bets, tackle the hard stuff, and view constraints as fuel, not friction.

  • 1% Better Every Day: You believe that small, consistent improvements lead to exponential growth. You move quickly, deliver results, and learn from every experience.

  • All In, All the Time: You show up and step up. You take ownership from start to finish and do what it takes to deliver when it counts.

  • People-Powered Greatness: You invest in your teammates. You give and receive feedback with care and candour. You build trust through high standards and shared success.

  • Grow the Whole Pie: You seek out win-win solutions for merchants, couriers, and our customers, because when they thrive, so do we.

    If these resonate, and you combine strong technical fundamentals with entrepreneurial drive, let’s connect.

Relay is an equal-opportunity employer committed to diversity, inclusion, and fostering a workplace where everyone thrives.

You will own the adoption and long-term success of 15 – 20 corporate accounts: building the relationships, defining the outcomes and serving as the trusted adviser who turns Legora into an embedded part of how those teams operate.

Mid-market means breadth as well as depth. You will lean on repeatable playbooks where they work and go bespoke where an account earns it.

For every account you will build a tailored roadmap, sequence initiatives from initial rollout through function-wide scaled adoption, define measurable outcomes and ROI and evolve the programme as new AI capabilities and use cases emerge.

Stora is looking for a Head of Sales to take ownership of the sales function as the business moves into its next stage of growth.

This is a hands-on leadership role, not a manage-from-the-sidelines one.

There is already a product customers want, an established position in the UK and Ireland, growing European opportunity, and a sales team in place. The challenge now is to turn that foundation into a more predictable, repeatable commercial engine.

You’ll work directly with the CEO, lead SDRs and Account Executives, improve how pipeline is created and converted, and bring greater clarity to forecasting, performance and where the next growth opportunities sit.

The opportunity

Stora has grown quickly, but the next stage requires more than simply doing more of what worked before.

The Head of Sales will be expected to answer questions like:

  • Where should the team focus its time and why?

  • How does outbound become consistently productive?

  • Where are deals getting stuck?

  • How should SDRs and AEs be coached and developed?

  • Which segments and markets represent the strongest opportunities?

  • What needs to change in the sales motion as Stora moves upmarket and expands internationally?

  • How does the business build a forecast leadership can genuinely rely on?

This is a role with real authority to improve things, alongside accountability for the results.

What you’ll own

  • Sales strategy and execution

  • Leadership, coaching and development of the SDR and AE team

  • Outbound performance and pipeline generation

  • Sales process from first engagement through to closed-won

  • Forecasting, pipeline health and revenue visibility

  • Performance management and clear expectations across the team

  • Key and strategically important opportunities where senior involvement can make a difference

  • Close alignment with Marketing and Product around ICP, messaging, customer insight and market opportunity

You’ll also stay close to customers and deals.

Stora wants a sales leader who knows what is happening on the ground, not someone whose understanding of the market comes entirely from dashboards and weekly reports.

What a strong candidate looks like

Stora needs a hands-on B2B SaaS sales leader who can build consistent performance, not just manage what already exists.

You’re likely someone who:

  • Has a genuine hunter mentality and knows how to create pipeline, not just manage what lands

  • Has led and developed SaaS sales teams and can raise the standard of performance around them

  • Knows what good outbound looks like and can coach it properly

  • Has personally sold into SMB and/or mid-market customers and can still step into important deals when needed

  • Builds healthier, more predictable pipeline and brings strong forecasting discipline

  • Qualifies hard, prioritises well and is comfortable walking away from weak opportunities

  • Uses data to improve decisions without hiding behind dashboards

  • Challenges assumptions, spots where the sales motion is weak and acts on it

  • Sets clear expectations, coaches directly and holds people accountable

  • Can move comfortably between commercial strategy with the CEO, coaching the team and getting involved in a deal that matters

  • Has the commercial instinct to spot new segments, markets or opportunities worth pursuing

This is still a stage where leadership means building as well as leading. If you want to inherit a large sales organisation, established territories and a finished playbook, this probably is not the role.

Experience in vertical SaaS, operationally complex industries or international markets would be useful, but none are essential.

Why Stora

Stora builds the software self storage operators use to run and grow their businesses, covering areas including bookings, payments, facility management, reporting and automation.

The business has established strong traction in the UK and Ireland and is continuing to expand across Europe and other international markets.

For a Head of Sales, that creates an interesting point to join:

  • Existing customers and market credibility

  • A sales team already in place

  • Significant European market opportunity ahead

  • Direct access to the CEO and leadership team

The foundations exist. The opportunity is to build what comes next.

Location

Stora operates as a distributed business across the UK and Europe.

ABOUT CODEWAY

 

We build and publish mobile apps that reach millions fast. 

 

We've built category-leading apps time and time again. A track record proven by hits like Cleanup (#1 iPhone storage cleaner worldwide), Retake AI (#1 AI face editing app in the US), and Learna AI (the top AI language learning app globally), alongside 50+ other apps across productivity, edtech, wellness, and entertainment, all shaping the future of consumer mobile.

 

Since launching in 2020 with a small team in Istanbul, we've grown into a 300+ person global team. With over 400 million downloads and a worldwide footprint, we're already one of the fastest-growing consumer tech companies in Europe, and join us in our next big chapter.

POSITION

 

As our Corporate FP&A Analyst - Planning, you will report directly to the Director of FP&A and sit at the ultimate strategic clearinghouse of our finance function. As our portfolio scales globally, we are building a lean, world-class decision-support function from the ground up to evaluate complex strategic options, portfolio expansions, and capital deployment choices. You will sit at the corporate level, owning the master consolidation, corporate budget, and the underlying logic for individual app-level P&Ls.


This is an AI-first, digital-native finance team. We communicate via active Slack channels, build out our operational blueprints and context sharing inside Notion, and run collaboration entirely through Google Workspace. You will leverage modern workflows—initially building and auditing multi-variable models in Microsoft Excel using the Claude for Excel add-in, with a direct, subsequent mandate to act as a core product stakeholder driving our platform migration to Pigment.



KEY SKILLS

To excel in this role, you must bring a sharp blend of institutional corporate finance discipline, modern data literacy, and a forward-looking technology stack:

  • Strategic Architecture: Mastery of 3-statement long-range planning (LRP), rolling monthly forecasting, and corporate top-down / bottom-up budget reconciliation.

  • Tactical Liquidity Control: Active management of short-term cash mechanics, specifically building 13-week rolling cash flow forecasts.

  • Next-Gen Financial Stack: Advanced driver-based Excel modeling paired with prompt engineering (Claude for Excel) and multi-dimensional EPM exposure (Pigment / Anaplan).

  • Data & Ledger Awareness: Familiarity or exposure to data systems (Looker / BI tools) and cloud ERP structures (NetSuite) to collaborate effectively on data alignment.

  • Mobile Ecosystem Domain Expertise: Deep familiarity with B2C mobile metrics (ROAS, LTV, CAC, and cohort curves) and institutional debt facility covenant tracking.



WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING

  • Own the Global Planning Cycle Engine & Budget Setting: Act as the architect and coordinator of Codeway’s global budget setting and forecasting process. You will build and own the corporate top-down strategic forecasting model and lead the continuous process of coordinating and consolidating the bottom-up inputs from the FBP network. You will design, establish, and push unified planning templates out to the FBPs, running a rigorous rolling monthly forecast to keep the global corporate model perfectly synchronised with live business pacing. You will partner closely with FBPs to challenge operational assumptions, extract key variables, and align strategic direction to fuel "The Engine."

  • Enterprise Valuation & Long-Range Planning (LRP): Build and scale corporate three-statement models and integrated multi-year cash flow frameworks explicitly designed to evaluate macro strategic options, support capital structuring, and drive long-term corporate value creation.

  • Tactility & Liquidity Control: Balance macro long-range planning with hyper-tactical operational control by owning, executing, and maintaining a tight, rolling 13-week cash flow forecast.

  • Corporate UA Integration & Capital Pacing: Partner closely with our Corporate FP&A team members who own the portfolio UA allocation models. While they evaluate cohort dynamics across our apps to maximise ROAS, you will integrate their marketing deployment outputs into our central business plan, reconciling portfolio allocation shifts directly against corporate cash reserves and growth capital constraints.

  • Growth Capital & Credit Facility Management: Direct the tracking, optimisation, and structural compliance of our institutional credit facility used to scale UA. Monitor global capital drawdowns, track funding velocity against strict covenant thresholds, and generate institutional-grade financial reporting for our lending partners.

  • Multi-Dimensional Portfolio Cost Allocations: Architect and manage the cost allocation framework required to distribute centralised overhead (shared engineering, global data lakes, corporate G&A) down to individual app-level P&Ls to isolate and report true fully loaded unit economics.

  • Advanced Scenario Modeling: Build dynamic, driver-based sensitivity models to instantly simulate shifting ecosystem dynamics and top-of-funnel marketing performance, cleanly integrating core growth metrics (ROAS, LTV, and CAC).

  • Board Preparation & Headcount Alignment: Synthesise complex data into premium corporate narratives and visual decks for quarterly board reviews. Partner closely with the Talent Acquisition (TA) team to ensure global hiring plans and recruitment velocity reconcile perfectly with approved corporate budget constraints.

  • System Integration & BI Collaboration: Support the connection between our corporate planning stack and underlying data environments. You will collaborate on projects to ensure financial actuals from NetSuite and core revenue performance/unit economics from Looker sync cleanly into our planning architecture (Excel/Claude → Pigment).



WHAT YOU’LL BRING

  • Experience: 3-6 years in Corporate FP&A, Strategic Finance, Investment Banking, or Transaction Advisory within a high-growth B2C digital platform, mobile app company, or gaming studio.

  • Dual-Speed Financial Fluency: Equal comfort building high-level strategic valuation structures (3-statement multi-year planning) and executing rapid, short-term liquidity controls.

  • Elite Individual Contributor Profile: A high-autonomy operator who executes with urgency. You are highly proactive, you drive projects forward independently, and take immense pride in the technical integrity of your models.

  • The Codeway Ethos: A natural self-starter who looks forward, not backward. You completely avoid an audit or ledger-heavy mindset; you treat finance as an agile, value-generating growth partner, and possess the conviction to challenge leadership constructively in a founder-led culture.

  • Collaborative Matrix Skills: Strong foundational background in corporate consolidation and recurring planning windows. You excel at extracting variables from decentralised partners, using high-impact communication to pressure-test assumptions and seamlessly turn operational data into continuous rolling monthly forecasts.

  • Mobile Ecosystem Domain Expertise: Deep operational understanding of app store economics, subscription models, digital revenue dynamics, and core growth tracking metrics—specifically ROAS, LTV, and CAC.

  • Next-Gen Technical Profile: You treat prompt engineering as a core finance capability, with hands-on experience or immediate adaptability to LLM add-in layers (Claude for Excel).

  • Systems & Data Literacy: Comfortable navigating Looker (or equivalent BI platforms) to view or cross-check revenue performance and tracking data frameworks within NetSuite. Exposure to multi-dimensional EPM tools (Pigment, Anaplan, or Workday Adaptive) is a major plus.



WHAT WE OFFER

 

  • Flexible Career Trajectory: We are looking for an exceptional builder. If leadership is your goal and you demonstrate the capability, this role is positioned on a direct track to step up and lead the Corporate FP&A team. Alternatively, if your passion lies in pure execution, you have the option to remain as a principal individual contributor driving global architecture.

  • Scale & Impact: The rare opportunity to shape the central financial architecture of a profitable, self-funded scale-up ($400M+ ARR) right at its inception.

  • Culture: An energetic, high-performance environment where finance is treated as an aggressive value-generator rather than administrative overhead. Relocation support available if you decide to move to Barcelona.

Meet DeepL

DeepL is a global AI product and research company focused on building secure, intelligent solutions to complex business problems. Over 200,000 business customers and millions of individuals across 228 global markets today trust DeepL's Language AI platform for human-like translation, improved writing and real-time voice translation.
Founded in 2017 by CEO Jaroslaw “Jarek” Kutylowski, DeepL now has around 1,000 passionate employees and is supported by world-renowned investors including Benchmark, IVP, and Index Ventures.

Our goal is to become the global leader in trusted, intelligent AI technology, building products that drive better communication, foster connections, and create a meaningful impact. To achieve this, we need talented people like you to join our journey. If you’re ready to shape the future of AI and grow your career in a fast-moving, purpose-driven environment, DeepL is your next destination.

What sets us apart

What sets us apart is our blend of cutting-edge AI technology, meaningful work, and a culture where people truly thrive. We’re a team of innovators, researchers, and creators driven by a shared purpose to unlock human potential by making work simpler, smarter, and more connected.

When we share what it’s like to work at DeepL, the reactions are overwhelmingly positive. This might be because of our technology that helps millions of people and businesses communicate and work better every day, or because of the trust, curiosity, and care that shape our culture.

What we know for sure is this: being part of DeepL means joining a team dedicated to innovation, growth, and well-being. Discover more about life at DeepL onLinkedIn,Instagram, and our Blog.

Meet the team behind this journey

You will join the Developer Experience track, whose customers are DeepL's own engineers. Every change that reaches our products, from a research prototype to a production release, travels through the platform, pipelines and workflows this track owns. Our job is to make that journey fast, safe and obvious, so that engineers spend their time on the problems only they can solve.

That ownership runs the full width of the developer's day. It covers the foundation: source control, the CI and CD fleet that runs every pipeline across Kubernetes, macOS and Windows, build and dependency caching, and the artifact and package registries that hold what we ship. Having recently moved our source and CI onto GitLab SaaS, we are now shaping what a genuinely self-service platform looks like on top of it.

It also covers everything an engineer actually touches: our internal developer portal and service catalogue in Backstage, the Golden Path templates and release automation that make the right thing the easy thing, automated guardrails for security and production readiness, self-service access management, and the AI tooling our engineers use every day, including AI-assisted code review. We measure whether any of it is working, through developer surveys and delivery metrics.

We treat developer experience as a product, not a support function. We are opinionated about paved roads, allergic to mandates without migration paths, and increasingly focused on a question the whole industry is still answering: what does an engineering organisation look like when AI is a first-class part of how software gets built?

Your responsibilities

  • Own technical direction for a significant part of the Developer Experience mandate. Identify where the biggest friction sits for our engineers, form a clear position on how to remove it, and see that work through to adoption.

  • Lead initiatives that lift developer productivity across multiple engineering teams, by understanding and improving processes and tooling, and by drawing on both established software engineering practice and AI capability.

  • Design and build the workflows and tooling that carry a change through the software development lifecycle, from local development through review to release.

  • Lead our work on AI across that lifecycle. Evaluate what genuinely helps, build the guardrails that make it safe and useful at our scale, and be candid about what does not work.

  • Treat internal developers as customers and grow a community around developer experience. Talk to them, watch where they struggle, and let evidence decide what to build and whether it landed, whether that evidence is survey data, delivery metrics or support load. Empower product teams to own their delivery journey, and turn consensus across engineering into shipped change. Much of the work at this level is influence without authority.

  • Define standards that hold across the track and drive migrations to them, bringing teams along with a working path rather than a deadline.

  • Mentor engineers across the track and raise the technical bar of the group, through design reviews, architecture decisions and the everyday habits that keep systems maintainable.

  • Share in operating what we build, including a sustainable on call rotation for the services and tooling other teams rely on.

Qualities we look for

  • A software engineering background, in any language, with real depth in at least one. We genuinely do not mind which: C#, Go, TypeScript and Python are all well represented here. We care that you can build software other engineers rely on, and that you can read your way into an unfamiliar codebase.

  • Time in a product team, shipping to external customers. The best developer experience work comes from people who have personally felt the pipeline they are now redesigning, and who know what a product team is actually optimising for.

  • Genuine passion for developer experience. Build systems, CI and CD, internal platforms, release engineering, and the texture of what makes a codebase pleasant or miserable to work in. This is a role for someone who finds this intrinsically interesting, not a stepping stone.

  • Enthusiasm for figuring out where AI creates real leverage in how software gets built, a willingness to run experiments that fail, and enough scepticism to tell the difference between a genuine improvement and a demo.

  • A track record of technical ownership spanning several teams. You create clarity where a mandate crosses team boundaries, hold clear positions, change them on evidence, and carry other engineers with you.

  • The judgement to trade the ideal solution for one you can ship and iterate on, and the tenacity to keep going. Changing how an engineering organisation works is a long game, and adoption is the hard part.

You would get bonus points for

  • Measuring developer productivity credibly, through DORA, developer surveys, or your own defensible approach.

  • Having built or operated AI-assisted developer tooling: code review, agents, MCP servers, or evaluation of any of the above.

  • Experience building an internal developer platform or portal, especially with Backstage.

  • Community building you can point to. Open source maintainership, a guild or community of practice, developer advocacy, or any place you have grown adoption and ownership rather than mandated it.

  • GitLab or comparable CI and CD at scale, and build system work on large polyglot codebases. Runner fleets, pipeline performance, caching and artifacts, and compile and test time optimisation.

What we offer

  • Diverse and internationally distributed team: joining our team means becoming part of a large, global community with people of more than 90 nationalities. We're more than just colleagues; we're a group of professionals with a shared mission to connect diverse cultures. Our global presence is growing–we've doubled in size nearly every year, with our employees based in the UK, Germany, the Netherlands, Poland, the US, and Japan, and we continue to expand our network.

  • Open communication, regular feedback: as a language-focused company, we value the importance of clear, honest communication. We value smooth collaboration, direct and actionable feedback, and believe that leading with empathy and growth mindset makes us better together.

  • Hybrid work, flexible hours: we offer a hybrid work schedule, with team members coming into the office twice a week. This allows you to engage directly with your team and experience the unique energy of our workspace, while still enjoying the flexibility and comfort of working from home. Meet DeepL

DeepL is a global AI product and research company focused on building secure, intelligent solutions to complex business problems. Over 200,000 business customers and millions of individuals across 228 global markets today trust DeepL's Language AI platform for human-like translation, improved writing and real-time voice translation.
Founded in 2017 by CEO Jaroslaw “Jarek” Kutylowski, DeepL now has around 1,000 passionate employees and is supported by world-renowned investors including Benchmark, IVP, and Index Ventures.

Our goal is to become the global leader in trusted, intelligent AI technology, building products that drive better communication, foster connections, and create a meaningful impact. To achieve this, we need talented people like you to join our journey. If you’re ready to shape the future of AI and grow your career in a fast-moving, purpose-driven environment, DeepL is your next destination.

What sets us apart

What sets us apart is our blend of cutting-edge AI technology, meaningful work, and a culture where people truly thrive. We’re a team of innovators, researchers, and creators driven by a shared purpose to unlock human potential by making work simpler, smarter, and more connected.

When we share what it’s like to work at DeepL, the reactions are overwhelmingly positive. This might be because of our technology that helps millions of people and businesses communicate and work better every day, or because of the trust, curiosity, and care that shape our culture.

What we know for sure is this: being part of DeepL means joining a team dedicated to innovation, growth, and well-being. Discover more about life at DeepL onLinkedIn,Instagram, and our Blog.

Meet the team behind this journey

A good translation is accurate. A translation an organisation can actually publish has to use their words, follow their style, and sound like them. That is what this team builds.

Customisation used to be a feature inside our translator. It is now a pillar of an enterprise platform. A customer's terminology, style rules and translation memory apply to documents and presentations, run inside multi step translation flows, and feed quality evaluation that understands which customisations were applied. It is one of the clearest reasons large organisations choose DeepL and stay with us.

We own that surface end to end: glossaries and terminology, style rules, style profiles and translation memory, along with the sharing and administration that let an organisation govern all of it. We work alongside a research team who build the models that apply a customer's voice to the translation itself, which makes this one of the more genuinely collaborative engineering roles at DeepL.

Your responsibilities

  • Lead, grow and develop a small, senior full stack team, and set its technical direction across services and the customer-facing web experience.

  • Own the customisation surface end to end: terminology and glossaries, style rules, style profiles, translation memory, and the sharing and administration around them.

  • Shape the product, not just deliver it. Work with your product manager and designer to define how customisation should actually feel to use, and bring a point of view of your own rather than waiting for a specification.

  • Challenge what we are shipping. The biggest wins available here are the unglamorous ones: making it possible to organise, find and trust a large set of customisations rather than being buried by them. We want someone who spots those and argues for them.

  • Take responsibility for whether customers use what we build, not just whether we ship it. Find out where people drop out of the journey and close those gaps.

  • Reduce the setup burden. Make configuring customisation something an administrator can do confidently on their own rather than something that needs weeks of guided onboarding.

  • Partner with our research colleagues to bring adaptive, context-aware personalisation from prototype into a product customers trust, including the transparency that lets them see why a translation was personalised.

  • Look after customer-owned assets properly. Glossaries and translation memories are what our customers have invested most in, and they need to be safe, portable and correctly scoped.

  • Work across research, product, design, platform, identity and go-to-market teams, and turn what customers are hitting into engineering priorities leadership can act on.

  • You have worked closely with product and design to define user experience, not just to receive requirements from it. You can point to a product decision that was better because you were in the room.

  • You challenge the brief. You have talked a team out of building the wrong thing, or into building something nobody had asked for, and you can explain how you made the case.

  • You have managed engineers on a customer-facing B2B product, and you can describe what changed for those customers as a result.

  • You are technically solid enough to earn the trust of very experienced engineers. You will not be the deepest person in the room on every topic, and you do not need to be, but you do need to hold your own in a design discussion.

  • You have owned an adoption or engagement problem and moved the number. You know the difference between shipping a capability and getting people to use it.

  • You have worked alongside a research or applied science team on a jointly developed feature, and you know how to make that handover work in both directions.

We design Spotify’s consumer experience—end to end, moment to moment, across every screen, platform, and partner integration. Our mission is to make listening feel effortless, personal, and joyful for billions of users around the world. That means turning complexity into clarity across hundreds of touchpoints—from our mobile and desktop apps to the smart speakers, TVs, cars, and integrations where Spotify shows up every day. If it touches a consumer, we shape it. We bring deep insight into human behavior, design, and technology to craft experiences that feel intuitive, expressive, and unmistakably Spotify.

We're looking for a Senior Product Designer to join the Partner and Platform Experience (PPX) team. You'll tackle problems where social dynamics, device ecosystems, and technical constraints intersect. It's work that demands systems thinking, deep comfort with technical complexity, and a drive to make complex interactions feel simple and engaging.

  • Design experiences that help listeners share moments together and move effortlessly between the devices and platforms around them.

  • Create thoughtful, polished user experiences with a strong focus on interaction design, visual craft, and the details that make an experience feel intuitive.

  • Use prototyping to explore, communicate, and test ideas, including AI-assisted and code-based approaches where they help us learn faster.

data.description:
About the team

SumUp is best known for helping small businesses get paid — our Consumer tribe builds the other half of that story. We make SumUp Consumer, the wallet app that lets everyday consumers pay SumUp merchants with a tap, send money to friends, track their spending and earn loyalty rewards along the way.

As we grow SumUp Consumer across new markets and features, we need sharp, reliable insight into how people discover, adopt and use the product — and how that behaviour translates into sustainable commercial growth. This includes understanding our acquisition funnel, improving activation and conversion, increasing customer value, and reducing churn.

We're looking for a Product Data Analyst to join the Consumer tribe and become the analytical partner for SumUp Consumer. You'll work closely with Product Managers, Designers and Engineers, alongside our Analytics Engineering team, to understand customer behaviour, shape product strategy, and connect product performance to business outcomes.

You'll help answer questions such as:

  • Which acquisition channels and customer segments generate the strongest long-term value?
  • Where do customers drop out of the journey from acquisition to activation?
  • What drives repeat usage, retention and churn?
  • Which product changes improve conversion, customer value or commercial performance?
  • How should we prioritise product investments across markets and customer segments?

If you're motivated by meaningful analytical work, enjoy translating complexity into clarity, and want to see your insights directly influence both product decisions and commercial outcomes, this role is for you.

What you'll do

  • Analyse customer behaviour and product performance across the full consumer lifecycle — from acquisition and activation through engagement, retention, churn and reactivation.
  • Identify opportunities to improve conversion, customer value and sustainable growth using funnel analysis, cohort analysis, segmentation and behavioural analytics.
  • Collaborate closely with Product Managers, Designers, Engineers and Data teams to ensure decisions are grounded in robust analysis, customer insight and commercial understanding.
  • Evaluate the performance of customer segments, markets, channels and product journeys, helping the team understand where growth opportunities and commercial trade-offs exist.
  • Support decisions that improve key business outcomes, such as activation, conversion, repeat usage, retention, churn, customer lifetime value and revenue-related metrics.
  • Conduct exploratory analysis to answer product and business questions, translating complex data into clear, commercially relevant recommendations.
  • Define, monitor and communicate core SumUp Consumer KPIs, covering acquisition, activation, engagement, conversion, retention, churn and customer value.
  • Design, execute and analyse A/B tests and product experiments, assessing both customer impact and commercial impact.
  • Build and maintain dashboards and reporting that stakeholders actively use, proactively surfacing trends, anomalies, performance risks and growth opportunities.
  • Help Product Managers assess the expected impact of opportunities and evaluate whether product investments are delivering the intended customer and business outcomes.
  • Partner with Analytics Engineering to ensure KPI definitions, business logic and product instrumentation are accurate, scalable and trusted.
  • Bring a curious eye to AI and machine learning techniques, including LLM-assisted analysis, to speed up insight generation, customer understanding and product measurement.

You'll be great for this role if…

  • You have strong SQL skills and are comfortable querying, analysing and validating data in a cloud data warehouse such as Snowflake, BigQuery or similar.
  • You have hands-on experience with product analytics techniques such as funnel analysis, cohort analysis, segmentation and behavioural analysis.
  • You understand the commercial drivers of a digital product, including customer acquisition, conversion, activation, retention, churn and customer lifetime value.
  • You can connect customer behaviour and product performance to business outcomes, and use data to identify growth opportunities and inform prioritisation.
  • You've worked on A/B tests or product experiments, with a solid grounding in the statistics behind them.
  • You're proficient in a visualisation tool such as Looker, Tableau or Power BI, with a track record of building dashboards that stakeholders actually use.
  • You can translate ambiguous product or business questions into structured analysis, and explain findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences alike.
  • You're comfortable assessing trade-offs, challenging assumptions and making recommendations based on evidence.
  • You're curious about how AI and emerging techniques can improve product measurement, experimentation, customer understanding and commercial decision-making.
  • You're comfortable managing multiple workstreams and stakeholders, with strong prioritisation and a proactive communication style.

This role does not support Visa sponsorship and candidates must have the right to work in the UK.

Why you should join SumUp

🌎 Opportunity to work with a truly global, multicultural team from our central London Bridge location, wrapped in historic charm and modern flair. This involves an office-first setup

🌈 Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion: be part of a workplace that values and promotes diversity, fostering an inclusive environment where everyone's perspectives are respected and embraced

🚀 Enrolment onto our Virtual Stock Option programme: you will own a stake in SumUp's future success

🏖 Generous time off: enjoy 28 days of paid leave, plus bank holidays and special leaves

📚 A dedicated annual L&D budget for attending conferences and/or advancing your career through further education

🏥 Health matters: private health insurance, including optical and dental

🚗 Life made easier: salary-sacrifice commuter benefits via Gogeta

💼 Financial security: retirement scheme (SumUp matches 7% when you contribute 5%)

🛡 Peace of mind: life insurance from MetLife for 2× your salary

🌴 Break4me: 1-month sabbatical after 3 years of service

🔗 Referral Bonus: earn additional rewards by referring talented individuals to join the SumUp team

About SumUp

Be empowered to do more that matters.

At SumUp, we're on a mission to empower small businesses across the globe by providing simple and affordable tools that allow them to thrive. Today, over 4 million businesses in 37 markets rely on SumUp as their financial partner to manage payments, finance and customer relationships.

Our commitment to small businesses is reflected in our diverse team of over 3,000 SumUppers from over 90 nationalities, united by global collaboration and an innovative mindset. Our core values lay the foundation for who we are and what we stand for, shaping our work culture and driving our success. We foster inclusivity and a continuous learning culture, providing a safe space for personal and professional growth. Our differences make us unique and strong as we strive to create an environment where everyone belongs and feels supported, no matter how they identify.

SumUp is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer, actively seeking and embracing diversity in our workforce. We don't make hiring or employment decisions based on race, colour, religion or religious belief, ethnic or national origin, nationality, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, age or any other basis protected by applicable laws or prohibited by company policy. Our commitment extends beyond recruitment to creating a safe and respectful workplace where harassment of any form is strictly prohibited. Discover more about our culture and opportunities on our careers website, and follow our journey on LinkedIn, Instagram, and TikTok.

Your new team:

As an Implementation Specialist, you are right at the heart of our projects: You translate business requirements into robust technical tracking solutions, implement them, ensure their quality, and turn concepts into fully functioning digital analytics setups. You take full responsibility for digital analytics implementations from initial requirements through to go-live and act as a trusted advisor to our clients throughout the process.


What awaits you:

  • You analyze our clients’ requirements and translate business and analytics use cases into technically sound tracking and implementation concepts.
  • You develop and document tracking concepts, data models, and data layer requirements and align them with clients and developers.
  • You work with tag management systems, implement tracking and third-party tags, and ensure scalable data collection.
  • You conduct technical testing, debugging, and data validation and systematically investigate data quality issues.
  • You consider consent management, data protection, and technical requirements from the very beginning of the implementation process.
  • You work closely with Digital Analysts, Data Engineers, and Project Managers, acting as the technical interface between business and development.
  • You actively share your expertise within your team and help develop our standards, best practices, and ways of working.
  • Depending on the project, you may also support tool selection, architecture decisions, migrations, and the technical enablement of our clients.


What you can expect:

At FELD M, you won’t work within a traditional agency structure with rigid specializations. We bring together different disciplines and perspectives and see ourselves as The Data Collective.

You will have the opportunity to work with a diverse range of clients, industries, and technology setups while continuously expanding your expertise. We deliberately work independently of specific tools while bringing many years of expertise and strong partnerships with, among others, Google and Adobe. Our projects range from auditing and optimizing existing implementations to complete new implementations and migrations, as well as complex analytics and data setups.

You also won’t work in isolation: At FELD M, the close connection between business, analytics, and technology is at the core of what we do. This intersection is what makes the role particularly exciting.

What else? We believe in People First and Sustainable Pace. Taking responsibility and delivering high-quality work does not mean constantly operating at full speed. We want to do great work sustainably – together, with mutual support and room for different lifestyles.We are looking for people who are curious, take ownership, and enjoy sharing their expertise. We don’t see job descriptions as rigid checklists. Instead, we want to understand how your experience, interests, and strengths fit the role and what we need as a team.


What you bring along:

  • You don’t need to know every tool. What matters more is that you have a strong understanding of digital analytics and can quickly familiarize yourself with new technologies and setups.
  • Several years of professional experience in digital analytics, web analytics, tracking, or MarTech implementation
  • Strong knowledge of at least one tag management system
  • Experience designing and implementing data layers and tracking concepts
  • A solid understanding of client-side and server-side tracking, as well as their respective technical requirements and capabilities
  • A solid technical understanding of web technologies, particularly JavaScript
  • Experience with testing and data validation of analytics implementations
  • An understanding of consent management, data protection, and the technical implications for tracking
  • The ability to explain technical concepts clearly to different stakeholders
  • A structured, analytical, and quality-oriented approach to your work
  • A genuine interest in taking ownership and not just analyzing technical challenges, but implementing solutions yourself
We look forward to meeting you!

Overview

PR steht vor einem strukturellen Bruch. Vertrauen verschiebt sich, Sichtbarkeit wird neu verteilt, KI wächst exponentiell. Wir bei getpress glauben, dass Reputation in den nächsten zehn Jahren der entscheidende Wettbewerbsvorsprung für Unternehmen wird. Und dass die Agentur, die das ernst nimmt, anders aussehen muss als die Agentur von gestern.

Deshalb bauen wir die PR Company der Zukunft. Outcome-getrieben statt Retainer-Stunden. KI-first statt KI-on-top. Automatisiert, wo es skaliert und menschlich, wo es wirklich zählt. Unser über 40 köpfiges Team aus Journalist*innen und PR-Strateg*innen hat seit 2017 die PR für 450+ der spannendsten Wachstumsunternehmen Europas gesteuert – und hat Hunger auf mehr.

Bist du dabei?


Deine Rolle

  • Strategisch und themensicher: Du entwickelst individuelle PR Strategien für Kunden aus dem B2B- und B2C-Bereich – mit klarem Fokus auf Themenplatzierung in relevanten Medien. Dabei bringst du journalistisches Denken und strategische Kommunikation zusammen.
  • Beratend auf Augenhöhe: Du steuerst die Kommunikation mit deinen Kund*innen professionell, planst vorausschauend (z. B. mit Quartalsplänen & KPIs) und baust langfristige Beziehungen auf. Du bringst proaktiv Themen ein – und entwickelst die Kommunikation deiner Kund*innen kontinuierlich weiter. Du bist Sparringspartner*in auf C-Level-Augenhöhe, nicht Auftragsempfänger*in.
  • Teamorientiert & offen: Du teilst dein Wissen, gibst und nimmst Peer-to-Peer-Feedback über alle Erfahrungslevel hinweg, ohne Gatekeeping, mit echtem Interesse an gemeinsamer Weiterentwicklung.
  • Vorne auf der AI Welle: Du arbeitest aktiv mit unserem internen AI-Stack. Recherche, Pitch-Vorbereitung, Themen-Scouting – wo Maschinen schneller sind, lassen wir sie machen. Du investierst die gewonnene Zeit in Substanz, Beziehungen und Kreativität.
  • Aktives Netzwerken: Du baust und pflegst belastbare Beziehungen zu Journalist*innen aus den wichtigsten Medien im DACH Raum und Europas.


Wer du bist

  • 4+ Jahre Erfahrung in der operativen PR, idealerweise im Agenturumfeld, und hast Kund*innen nachweislich eigenständig in deutschen Leit- und Fachmedien platziert.
  • Du bringst fundierte Beratungskompetenz mit, analysierst Zielgruppen und Märkte, übersetzt Unternehmensziele in PR Strategien, leitest messbare Maßnahmen ab und begleitest deine Kund*innen als verlässliche* Sparringspartner*in auf Augenhöhe.
  • Du hast ein belastbares Netzwerk zu Journalist*innen und weißt, wie man vertrauensvolle Beziehungen aufbaut und pflegt.
  • Du beobachtest die Nachrichtenlage aktiv und erkennst Themenpotenziale, bevor andere sie auf dem Schirm haben.
  • Du arbeitest eigenverantwortlich, bringst dich ins Team ein und teilst dein Wissen offen.
  • Du nutzt KI-Tools pragmatisch, um Prozesse zu beschleunigen, damit mehr Zeit für inhaltliche Tiefe und kreative Ideen bleibt.
  • Du sprichst Deutsch auf C2- Niveau, kannst auch auf Englisch professionell kommunizieren und lebst in Deutschland


Was dich erwartet

  • Journalistische PR statt Massenversand: Bei uns gibt es keine generischen Pressemitteilungen oder Gießkannenverteiler. Wir arbeiten individuell, redaktionell und mit klarer Themenstrategie und pitchen gezielt per Telefon bei passenden Journalist*innen aus einem breiten Medienspektrum.
  • Langfristige Perspektive & Entwicklung: Du startest mit einem unbefristeten Vertrag. Gemeinsam entwickeln wir einen klaren Fahrplan für deine fachliche und persönliche Weiterentwicklung – mit regelmäßigen Feedbacks und transparenten Zielen.
  • Flexibilität, die wirklich gelebt wird: Ob remote, hybrid oder im Berliner Office – wir ermöglichen Arbeitsmodelle, die sich mit deinem privaten und beruflichen Leben gut vereinbaren lassen. Entscheidungsfreiheit, Eigenverantwortung und klare Kommunikation gehören für uns selbstverständlich dazu.
  • Unterstützung und offene Arme: Wir begegnen einander auf Augenhöhe – offen, ehrlich und mit echtem Interesse am Gegenüber. Wir lernen voneinander, geben einander Rückhalt und feiern gemeinsame Erfolge.
  • Eine Kultur von Challengern. Wir arbeiten ergebnisgetrieben, feiern Erfolge und erwarten, dass du uns challenged – und wir challengen zurück. Augenhöhe heißt bei uns: ehrliches Feedback in beide Richtungen.
  • Eine Lernkurve, die du anderswo nicht bekommst. Du arbeitest täglich mit einem Team, das das fortschrittlichste AI PR System im Markt baut. Wer sich jetzt einbringt, baut sich ein Profil, das in der Branche selten ist.
  • Benefits und Sweet Treats: Du kannst aus drei frei wählbaren Sachbezügen wählen, von einer betrieblichen Altersvorsorge mit 20% Zuschuss auf deine Einzahlungen profitieren,180 Tage im Jahr aus dem EU Ausland arbeiten, dich auf regelmäßige Teamevents freuen. Und das Beste: Du startest mit 27 Urlaubstagen aber je länger du bei uns bist, desto mehr Urlaubstage bekommst du dazu.


Unser nächsten Schritte

Wenn du jetzt denkst: ,,Klingt nach mir!’’, dann bewirb dich ohne Anschreiben bei uns und wer weiß, vielleicht bist du schon schneller als gedacht Teil unseres getpress-Teams!

Wir setzen uns für Chancengleichheit ein und begrüßen Bewerbungen von Menschen unabhängig von Geschlecht, Herkunft, Religion, sexueller Orientierung, Alter oder Behinderung.

Wir freuen uns dich kennenzulernen!

Dein People & Culture Team

  • You will collaborate on the design, development, deployment and maintenance of our web application, utilising modern technologies while adhering to industry best practices
  • You will work autonomously and contribute to architectural decisions alongside your team
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to build impactful solutions for the climate sector
  • Improve development workflow and contribute to building an efficient, high-performance engineering culture
  • Leverage AI coding tools as a core part of your development workflow to ship faster and maintain high code quality


Your Talent

  • You have at least 5+ years of software development experience
  • Strong expertise in React, Python, FastAPI, React, Redux Toolkit, and TanStack Router
  • Comfort using AI coding tools to accelerate development
  • Experience building AI-powered features
  • Experience in developing complex forms using react-hook-form and zod while ensuring a responsive and frictionless user journey
  • Proficiency in Tailwind CSS and modern UI development practices
  • You can evaluate what’s hype versus what’s real business value
  • You have a good understanding of Docker, AWS and cloud native architecture
  • You have experience debugging and resolving production issues
  • You have led large complex projects from beginning to end
  • You have excellent communication skills in English, and experience with distributed teams is a plus


Our Offer

Growth & Culture
We move fast, we're building a lot from scratch, and we're learning something new every day. You'll be part of a team that doesn't just work, it truly builds something, with a strong sense of ownership and genuine team spirit.

Impact
Your job has a direct impact on the energy transition. Period.
And because this is important to us, we offer extra days off for climate activism.

Flexibility
We work in a hybrid, trust-based environment.
Working from home is the norm for us, two days a week are standard and flexible. We structure the rest in whatever way best supports collaboration and focus within the team.
And if it works for you and your team, you can also work from other locations, workations are possible here.

Perks
You'll receive a flexible bonus that you can use however you like, sports, culture, travel, whatever works for you.

Food & Energy
Long days happen. When the office is running, so is the food: just order something to the office via Wolt.

Team & Vibe
We take our mission seriously, but we don't take ourselves too seriously.
Offsites, team nights, and our "Bees & Beers" are just as much a part of the job as the work itself.
